// workshops

AI Special Topic Workshops

One-hour, presenter-ready sessions in browser slide decks.

1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Can You Tell If It's AI? Watermarking Explained

Since August 2026 most AI text carries a hidden mark. What that mark actually is, watched one word at a time; why it survives copy and paste but not a code tidy-up; the EU rule that made it worldwide; why a detector result is never proof of who wrote something; and a playground where you watermark a passage and then detect it yourself.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Which AI Is Best? Reading the Scoreboard Like a Pro

Why "which AI is best?" has no fixed answer: the Turing test's quiet ending, how benchmarks work and die, whose scores to trust, and how to spot an app faking it. Ends with a cracking investigative video.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Growing Up Digital: An AI World Tour

How AI is growing up differently around the world: UNESCO readiness check-ups for six of the Territory's homeland countries, the global trust story, and a surprising data portrait of how Australians really use AI.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Bubble Trouble: Making Sense of the AI Economy

Is AI a bubble? Why the question has no tidy answer: circular financing, the US-China chip contest, information warfare and a military arms race; and what it all means for NT organisations.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

The Price of Thinking: AI Subscriptions and the New Digital Divide

The third digital divide: who gets premium AI plus instruction, who gets left out, what enterprise AI really costs, and the WhatsApp school that reached students the platforms couldn't.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Your Brain on Autocomplete: Why Writing Still Matters

What happens to thinking when AI does the writing? New brain research on "cognitive debt", plus five thousand years of writing history; clay tablets, scribes and one very sassy Mesopotamian.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Where Does Your Chat Go? Taking Care of Your Data in AI Tools

From surveillance capitalism and Cambridge Analytica to today's AI privacy settings: what "train our models" really means, the platform-by-platform guide, and what never to type at all.
1-hour workshop · Browser slides

Beyond the Buzzword: What Does AI-Literate Actually Mean?

AI literacy taken apart: how it differs from digital literacy, what the research scales really measure, a letter from an imagined 2026 graduate, and Australia's new guide to declaring your AI use.
// training games

Training Games

Presenter-driven games for live sessions; the room calls out the answers.

Presenter game · Browser, offline-ready

Prompt Critics: Excel with Copilot

Eight everyday Excel questions from a Northern Territory council are about to be sent to Copilot, and every one has a problem. The room calls it out before the send button gets pressed, the prompt gets fixed on screen, and the session ends with the Prompt Critic's checklist.
Presenter game · Browser, offline-ready

Prompt Critics: Darwin Business Excel

Thirteen everyday Excel questions from businesses around Darwin, a Parap cafe, a Berrimah transport yard, a harbour cruise operator, are about to be sent to Copilot, and every one has a problem. The room calls it out, the prompt gets fixed on screen, and the session closes with the Prompt Critic's checklist. Built as the entertaining finish to an Excel workshop.
// presentations

Presentations

Short, self-contained presentations on cybersecurity, AI literacy and digital skills topics; 30 minutes to an hour each. They run entirely in your browser: no PowerPoint, no downloads, no installs.

Presentation · 18 slides

Using AI in Excel: From Copilot Chat to Add-ins

Where Copilot helps in a spreadsheet, where it quietly gets things wrong, and how to check its work.
Presentation · 19 slides

How Scammers Fake It with AI

Voice cloning, deepfake endorsements, spoofed websites and the fake casinos targeting NT communities; and the habits that still beat all of them.
Presentation · 14 slides

Australia’s AI Laws: What’s Coming

What is actually law, what is guidance, and what the Territory has done about it.
Interactive deck · 14 slides

Is This a Scam? Ask an AI

One habit, taught by doing: copy the message that feels off, paste it into an AI assistant, and ask. Two scenarios run live in the deck.
Interactive deck · 4 modules

Why the Frontend Gate Fails, and the Real One Doesn't

Build the passcode gate an AI assistant writes for you, break it yourself in about ten seconds, then see what real access control does differently.
Interactive deck · 4 modules

From Ranking to Being Cited

What machines actually read on your site, why llms.txt is not the standard it is claimed to be, and what the research shows earns a citation.
Interactive deck · 5 modules

Putting a Website Online, Explained

The domain name you rent, the host that serves your files, the DNS that connects the two, and the certificate that locks it.
Presentation · 13 slides

MFA and Account Security

How passwords get out, the three kinds of proof a sign-in can ask for, and why number matching beats tap-to-approve.
Interactive deck · 4 modules

Mermaid: Diagrams You Write Instead of Draw

Why drawn diagrams go out of date, and the small text language that renders as one instead.
Interactive deck · 7 modules

Are You a Robot? CAPTCHAs Explained

Why the pictures of buses exist, what they were really training, and what replaced them.
Interactive deck · 5 modules

How Email Works

What happens between pressing send and the message arriving, and why that explains almost every impersonation attack you will ever see.
Interactive deck · 5 modules

Can I Print This? How 3D Printing Actually Works

What it really takes to turn a photo of a character into a solid plastic object: two printing technologies, a size limit nobody expects, and a food-safety catch.
Interactive deck · 6 modules

Can You Tell If It’s AI? Watermarking Explained

Why an AI text watermark is not a hidden character to strip out, how the green-list and red-list mechanism works, what happens when a detector is treated as proof, and a playground to run the mark yourself.
Interactive deck · 4 modules

Cognitive Uploading: Thinking with a Second Brain

A tour of Gemini Notebook, the hoarding habit it is meant to break, and the contested pedagogy behind source-grounded AI: does it help you think, or think instead of you?
Interactive deck · 3 modules

Ancient Plagiarism: A Thought Experiment

Humans have always built new texts out of older ones, from the Gilgamesh flood to the Synoptic Gospels. Plagiarism versus intertextuality, and what that long history changes about the anxiety over AI writing.
Interactive deck · 3 modules

AI Detectors and the Base-Rate Trap

What AI-writing detectors actually do, and the number trap that makes their scores so easy to misread. Includes a live base-rate calculator that shows honest students piling up in the flagged column.
Interactive deck · 4 modules

The Learning Science Behind Study and Learn

Microsoft says its Study and Learn agent is built on learning science. This deck reads the white paper closely: what the design gets right, and the gap between designed on the science and proven to improve learning.

About this site

NT World Ink holds the course materials, workshop decks and simulation tools used in cybersecurity, AI literacy, Microsoft Office and workplace digital skills training. Most courses come with Word handouts and practice files, so they can be run offline and away from this site.
